headline: Multiparametric and scaling readouts define neural state labels from observed dynamics
label: Neural State Inference From Observables
summary: Recent preprints and a published study define neural states from time-resolved, multiparametric, and scaling readouts, raising identifiability questions.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the assignment of discrete or scalar state labels to neural dynamics from structured observables, with state definitions dependent on chosen readouts and model structure. A time-resolved, multiparametric framework classifies electrode-level responses in neuronal cultures as excited, inhibited, or unchanged. A generalized Taylor's law with RMS scaling, applied to detrended fMRI, links the scaling exponent to synchrony and reports shifts across lifespan and in ADHD. DyssomniaNN couples two-process sleep regulation, hypothalamic flip-flop circuitry, and corticothalamic LIF networks to model human sleep disorders and perceived restedness. The items are heterogeneous; the third is a constrained mechanistic model. What is new is the use of multiparametric, time-resolved, or generalized scaling readouts to define states, alongside a multi-scale spiking model addressing perceived restedness. Whether such labels and parameters are identifiable from the available observables remains the open question.
